title: Optimize walkthrough: quant profiles INT8 vs FP8 - ByteWave
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked ByteWave through Optimize quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8), showed quality vs latency tradeoffs on sample benchmarks, discussed hardware constraints, recommended pilot on customer's dataset, and agreed next steps to run a 24h benchmark and share detailed pricing and security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-30 15:00 PST | Duration: ~47m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jamal (Product) // Evan (ByteWave CTO), Sofia (ML Eng), Marcus (Infra)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood, with Priya and Jamal. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Evan: Good thanks, excited to dig in. We demoed your API a bit last week but today we want to focus on Optimize - specifically quantization profiles, INT8 and FP8, and how that affects our latency/quality tradeoffs.
[00:25] Priya: Great, that's perfect. Quick agenda - we'll run through the high-level differences, show benchmark slides on quality vs latency, then talk about pilot/runbook for ByteWave. We'll also surface where hardware limits change the expectation.
[00:38] Sofia: Sounds good. We're particularly worried about hallucination rates - if we go lower precision will our hallucination go up for instruction-following tasks?
[00:48] Priya: Yes, good callout. Short answer: depends on profile and model architecture. INT8 often gives 2-3x latency improvement at cost of small quality drop on many open models; FP8 tends to preserve quality much better and still gives good latency, but support depends on kernel level and the runtime.
[01:10] Jamal: I'll share screen with the Optimize deck - slide 3 is the quality vs latency scatter we ran on the benchmark suite.
[01:18] Alex: Note - these are representative numbers on our internal eval suite, we also ran customer-specific tests for similar workloads, results vary by prompt length and batch size.
[01:27] [01:30] Priya: Ok slide: you can see baseline FP16 at ~95 quality score, latency 120ms/token. INT8 profile reduces latency to ~50-60ms/token but quality drops to ~88-90 depending on the prompt. FP8 sits at ~75-85ms/token with quality ~93-94.
[01:52] Evan: So FP8 is kind of the middle ground - better than INT8 in quality but not as fast as INT8. What are the failure modes - e.g., hallucinations, token repetition?
[02:04] Priya: Right - in our error analysis INT8 introduces slight calibration shifts and more conservative token probs which can increase repetition or make responses shorter; hallucination spike is usually small but shows up on long-context reasoning. FP8 preserves dynamic range better, so fewer weird calibration errors.
[02:24] Marcus: Hardware question - does FP8 require specific GPUs or drivers? We run on-prem A100s and some Ampere instances, and some L4/RTX fleet.
[02:36] Priya: FP8 is increasingly supported in newer kernels - on GPUs without hardware FP8 support we emulate FP8 which reduces perf gains. For A100 we get good INT8 and decent FP8 with optimized kernels; Hopper and newer have improved FP8 paths.
[02:58] [03:10] Sofia: Any weird interactions with KV cache / streaming? We do a lot of chat agents with long KV cache usage.
[03:18] Priya: Good question - KV-cache is orthogonal but precision of KV vectors matters. We do prefix caching in FP16 for stability by default and only quantize the compute path tokens; that keeps latency gains while reducing quality regressions for long-context. There's sometimes a switch to quantize KV cache for more savings but it increases quality risk.
[03:42] Alex: Quick demo: I'll run the same prompt in three profiles (FP16 baseline, INT8, FP8) - you'll see timings in the console.
[03:52] [04:00] Alex (screen): Running prompt: 'Summarize the following policy doc and list open questions' - FP16: 120ms/token, result length ~230 tokens, salience high.
[04:20] Alex: INT8: 55ms/token, result shorter, a couple minor omissions - you can see lower recall on named entities.
[04:30] Alex: FP8: 78ms/token, very close to FP16 on recall, a tiny formatting glitch, overall much better than INT8 for this prompt.
[04:45] Evan: That's helpful. For our production SLAs we need p95 latency under 200ms for single-turn customer queries - can we meet that with INT8?
[04:57] Priya: Yes, with batching and the right instance size INT8 is usually well under that p95 for single-turn. For multi-turn with KV it's trickier; FP8 + prefix caching often hits a safer p95 while keeping cost down vs FP16.
[05:14] [05:30] Marcus: Cost question - how do you price these? Is INT8 cheaper in hosted vs dedicated?
[05:38] Jamal: Billing is usage-based. For hosted API you get per-token with discounts available for quantized models in Optimize recommendations; Dedicated is committed capacity so unit economics change with reserved GPU families. We can model cost per 1M tokens per profile in the pilot.
[05:55] Priya: Also worth noting: Redwood Optimize will recommend profiles automatically based on latency/quality SLOs and can roll profiles by route.
[06:08] [06:30] Sofia: Can you walk through the benchmark methodology - how you measure 'quality score'?
[06:36] Priya: Sure - our quality score is a composite: weighted precision/recall on labeled eval sets, human-rated coherence (sampled), and a task-specific metric when available (e.g., F1 for extraction). It's not perfect but useful for relative comparisons. For customers we always run a dataset-specific eval.
[06:58] Evan: For our use case, entity extraction accuracy is critical; if INT8 drops F1 by 3-4 points that's unacceptable.
[07:08] Priya: Understood - we'll run extraction-focused eval in the pilot and recommend profiles that keep F1 within your target.
[07:18] [07:30] Alex: I'll open the 'profiles' tab in Console to show how to create a profile and schedule a rollout - small canary, 10% traffic, monitor quality metrics and error rates.
[07:45] [08:00] Alex (screen): Here we define profile: Model variant + quantization (INT8/FP8) + batching policy + fallback (auto to FP16 on errors). Then you can define alerts if quality drops.
[08:16] Jamal: We also support auto-fallback by policy - if the model fails to meet quality threshold or latency rises above SLO, traffic moves to a pinned variant.
[08:30] Sofia: How invasive is integration? We need to avoid changing too much of our infra.
[08:36] Alex: Minimal - for hosted API it's a drop-in. For Dedicated/Private we have agents and a config layer; no code changes needed for standard routes, just a config change to enable a profile. Marcus: That's good to hear.
[08:56] [09:15] Evan: Security question - we need SOC2 and KMS integration for keys. Also audit logs per token.
[09:23] Jamal: Redwood supports SOC 2, SAML SSO, per-token audit logs, and KMS integrations (customer-managed keys). We'll share the security packet after this call.
[09:34] Priya: We can also run PII redaction flows and show you the logs retention options in Private deployments.
[09:43] [10:00] Alex: Back to benchmarks - I'll walk through a sample CSV of results we ran on an LLM family. Slide shows latency histograms across profiles; notice p95 improvement from FP16->INT8 is substantial but variance increases.
[10:20] Priya: Important to calibrate expectations: INT8 tends to have lower median latency but a heavier tail in some workloads, depending on batching and instance type. FP8 usually gives a more predictable tail while still saving cost.
[10:40] Evan: Is there any model architecture that's particularly poor with INT8?
[10:46] Priya: Very deep decoder-only models with large MLPs can have quantization sensitivity; also models with complex normalization layers can behave oddly. We test per-model.
[10:58] [11:15] Sofia: Do you support mixed precision per-layer profiles? Like keep attention layers FP16 and quantize MLPs?
[11:25] Priya: Yes - Optimize supports per-layer and per-op profiles. Often quantizing MLPs gives most perf win while keeping attention in higher precision preserves model behavior. We show a recommended per-layer profile after the pilot.
[11:43] Alex: I'll paste a link in chat to the quant-profiles slide deck and the benchmark sheet (Drive link).
[11:50] [12:00] Alex (chat): Link: https://redwood.ai/optimize/quant-profiles-deck (placeholder)
[12:06] Evan: Great, we'll review that. One more thing - inference library compatibility, e.g. Triton or custom runtime?
[12:14] Priya: Redwood runtime integrates with Triton and our custom kernels; for Dedicated you can opt for our runtime or a Triton adapter. If you run in Private we support your runtime with a connector.
[12:28] [12:45] Marcus: About pilot logistics - how long to run a meaningful test?
[12:52] Priya: Usually 1-2 weeks with a representative dataset; for throughput or stability we recommend a 24-72 hour stress run plus mixed-traffic day-to-day. You asked about entity extraction - we'll run a 24h focused run with your sample set and the extraction metric.
[13:08] Evan: That timeline works. We'll need a scoped list of prompts and the dataset location.
[13:15] Alex: We'll follow up with a data ingestion link and instructions. We'll anonymize anything if needed.
[13:22] [13:30] Sofia: Are there any gotchas around tokenization differences when switching quant profiles?
[13:38] Priya: Tokenization is independent of quantization; however when quantization impacts model probabilities you may see slight tokenization-induced differences in outputs. We recommend fixed tokenizer config and seed across tests.
[13:52] [14:10] Alex: Ok demo part 2 - here's a small 'edge case' prompt that caused issues in INT8 in our prior runs. Running... INT8 returns truncated list items, FP8 returns full list, FP16 returns full list and better ordering.
[14:34] Evan: That's consistent with our earlier manual tests.
[14:40] Priya: We'll run a focused case-by-case analysis in the pilot and tag problematic prompts so you can either route them to FP16 or apply prompt engineering.
[14:52] [15:10] Marcus: For Dedicated reserved capacity - if we commit to a capacity, can we get a custom kernel build?
[15:18] Jamal: Yes, enterprise deals can include optimizations and custom kernel tuning for your model family. That usually happens after initial pilot.
[15:28] [15:40] Evan: Any competitors we should be aware of on the perf/cost front?
[15:45] Alex: Competitors we see are Lambda Labs for self-hosting, and some cloud providers' managed endpoints; OpenAI and Anthropic are more model-host oriented. We'll share a short competitor comparison doc.
[15:58] [16:10] Sofia: Do you have examples of customers who moved from INT8 -> FP8 or vice versa in production?
[16:18] Priya: Yes - a couple of fintech customers started on INT8 for throughput, then moved to FP8 for better quality on long-context risk analysis while keeping costs below FP16.
[16:32] Alex: We'll add anonymized case notes in the follow-up.
[16:38] [16:55] Evan: Ok logistics - what do you need from us to start the pilot?
[17:02] Alex: Ideally: 1) sample dataset (anonymized), 2) target metrics (p95 latency, F1 thresholds), 3) a contact for infra access if Dedicated/Private is desired. We'll provide a test endpoint and ingestion instructions.
[17:18] [17:30] Priya: We'll also provision a pilot dashboard in Console with the eval metrics and rollouts.
[17:38] Marcus: Security docs?
[17:41] Jamal: We'll email SOC2 and KMS integration docs and the data handling playbook after this call.
[17:48] [18:00] Alex: A couple of quick Qs from the chat - question: can Optimize do automatic profile switching by route? Answer: yes, per-route profile mapping available.
[18:15] Sofia: Great. One more technical - how do you handle mixed batch sizes from clients?
[18:22] Priya: Redwood runtime does dynamic batching and can apply batching policies per route; Optimize recommends batch targets that balance latency vs throughput. For interactive apps you can set low-latency small-batch policies.
[18:40] [19:00] Alex: We're nearing the end - recap and next steps.
[19:05] Alex: Next steps: we'll run a 24-hour focused benchmark (Priya), share quantization guide + pricing + security docs (Jamal), set up pilot dashboard and test endpoints (Alex).
[19:20] Evan: Sounds good. Can we get the benchmark started by next Tuesday?
[19:25] Priya: Yes we can target next Tuesday start, results within a week.
[19:30] [19:45] Action items noted in chat.
[20:00] Closing pleasantries, end of call.

Notes on transcription quality: auto transcript with occasional word swaps (e.g., 'K V cash' for KV cache) and missing punctuation.
